newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler clarifies status on service offer.
newsitem.headline: Daimler clarifies status on service offer.

text.p: Germany's Daimler-Benz AG, maker of luxury Mercedes cars, on Tuesday clarified that a recent offer of free servicing on Mercedes braking systems was not an official recall.
Daimler had said on August 7 it was offering a customer service measure for 176,000 vehicles worldwide due to problems with their braking systems.
In affected vehicles the brakes could overreact to a slight push on the brake pedal. Cars needed to be brought to garages for new components to be installed, the company said.
A spokesman for the company clarified on Tuesday that this operation could not be described as an official recall, but rather as a "customer service measure".

An official recall, which has to be registered with appropriate authorities, would be made only if there were a defect in a component which affected the safety of the vehicle, he said. This was not the case in this instance.
The brake system problem affects a series of Mercedes models, and was first noticed in the S-class luxury saloon and the SL cabriolet at the end of 1996.
Since March, the E-class executive range and since June the C-class saloon and CLK cabriolet have also been diagnosed with the defect. New brake sensors are now being built into cars in production.

The Mercedes braking system was designed to recognise emergency situations and engage at full power. Accident research has shown that drivers often do not step on the brakes hard enough to avoid accidents, the spokesman explained.
Of the total, some 88,000 vehicles are affected in Germany and can be repaired for free, Daimler said.
